liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): The Not Fade Away snippet includes a nice St. Stephen jam; Very strong, with a full St. Stephen jam rather than a mere tease [6][8]
- **Midnight Hour** (2 reviews): The Midnight Hour jam drifts into I Know You Rider and China Cat, then returns to finish; Rocking version with a China Cat jam inside it [7][8]
- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue//** (2 reviews): Baby Blue is described as moving and mature; Reviewer's favorite Baby Blue: superb Bobby noodling on his Gibson ES, churchy Pigpen organ, soulful Jerry vocal [6][8]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer singles out a nice Uncle John's Band [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **intro/a few million adjustments/while we're waiting for Pigpen**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [18]
- **Wake Up Little Suzie**: rare: 9 archived performances [18]
- **Swing Low Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [18]
- **Working Man's Blues**: rare: 14 archived performances [18]
- **If You Hear Me When I'm Leaving**: rare: 3 archived performances [18]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [18]
- **Superman**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [18]
- **All I Ever Wanted**: rare: 9 archived performances [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-06-04.123798.gdnrps.sonyTC124.olsen.droncit.flat.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 42 songs; 211 min; rated 4.33/5 by 9 [1]
- **gd1970-06-04.119921.sbd.acou.unk.miogi.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 51 min; rated 4/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Jerry's voice sounds very sweet on this acoustic-set soundboard recording; Jerry's voice sounds especially sweet and lovely in this session [12][13]
- **gd70-06-04.sbd.miller.12135.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 24 min; rated 4.1/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Good recording with guitars out front; Bobby is high in the mix; Only the end of the show circulates; jamming is tight, drums crisp, organ sounds good [6][11]
- **gd1970-06-04.123799.mtx.olsen.droncit.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 143 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [2]

## Around the show

- The band played before a hometown crowd [10]
- Reviewer's first Fillmore visit and first Grateful Dead show, on a summer night in San Francisco [16]
- Thursday admission was $3; the home crowd was satisfied after Baby Blue, and the band had three more nights that weekend [1]
- Gerry says Baby Blue calmed things down nicely, so there was no further encore [1]
- David Nelson and John "Marmaduke" Dawson are noted as joining the band on some songs [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-06-04.123798.gdnrps.sonyTC124.olsen.droncit.flat.flac16**: taped by Gerry Olsen; transferred by Dan McDonald and dusborne; source: Audience Recording by Gerry Olsen. Sony TC-124 single-capstan portable cassette deck equipped with Sony F-99S One Point Stereo Dynamic Microphone IMP LOW… [1]. Also: Filename credits a Sony TC124 recorder, Olsen, and droncit; the show also featured NRPS and Southern Comfort [1]
- **gd1970-06-04.119921.sbd.acou.unk.miogi.flac16**: taped by unknown; transferred by miogi; source: sbd > ?? > wav > audacity(snaps,crackles,pops) > wavmerge > cdwav > tlh(flaclevel8) > flac16 [3]. Also: Soundboard acoustic-set recording with an unknown amount missing [3]
- **gd70-06-04.sbd.miller.12135.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Reviewer taped the show on cassettes and digitized them, with flips, tape breaks, late starts and cut applause; Only Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour and Baby Blue circulate from the soundboard, in circulation since 1985 [4][16]
- **gd1970-06-04.123799.mtx.olsen.droncit.dusborne.flac16**: taped by Gerry Olsen; transferred by Dan McDonald and dusborne; source: Matrix of Soundboard (shnid:119921) sbd > ?? > wav > audacity(snaps,crackles,pops) > wavmerge > cdwav > tlh(flaclevel8) > flac16; conversion by: miogi;… [2]
